classification.difficultyReason: Identify opposite sectors from actual straight-line arm pairs, including diagrams with a third line.

content.prompt: Identify the vertically opposite angle to $\angle FGH$ in these diagrams.

spec.description: Unshaded wide X, with F and H above, B and A below, and G above the intersection.
spec.mathematics: F–G–A and B–G–H are straight lines.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer or angle marks in the question.

answer.worked: $GF$ and $GA$ are opposite rays; $GH$ and $GB$ are opposite rays. The vertically opposite angle is $\angle BGA$.

spec.description: Upright unshaded X, G labelled immediately left.
spec.mathematics: F–G–P and H–G–O are straight lines.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer or angle marks in the question.

answer.worked: $GF$ and $GP$ are opposite rays; $GH$ and $GO$ are opposite rays. The vertically opposite angle is $\angle OGP$.

spec.description: Two steep intersecting lines; F above-left, R above-right, H below-left, T below-right.
spec.mathematics: F–G–T and H–G–R are straight lines.
spec.answerVisibility: No answer or angle marks in the question.

answer.worked: $GF$ and $GT$ are opposite rays; $GH$ and $GR$ are opposite rays. The vertically opposite angle is $\angle RGT$.
